chapter: Mary Collins on Jelly Roll Morton and Willie the Lion
title: Mary's letter to a magazine about Willie the Lion Smith
summary: Mary describes her letter rebutting Willie the Lion Smith's remarks about Jelly Roll Morton, and Russell adds that Morton was accused of copying.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: ¶¶ Mr. Willie Linesmith. I called him, I said, Mr. Lion or Mr. Mouse. Oh, you should read this letter. Did you send a copy?

Huh? Did you send a copy yourself? No, I mean, but I mean. Do you still have a copy of what you're sending? Oh, no, I didn't pay no attention to that. You should have made a carbon copy. Yeah, sure. That should be coming up.

Oh, I just woke the man, I told him, I said, man, I've been buying your magazine for 15 years. I said, please, I actually have a special favor. Please print this letter for me. Mr. Mouse. Man, the boy I drug with. I sure hope he puts it up. He pointed me up, you know what I mean. I just hate to see a man talk that way about another man. You know what I mean. You don't have to talk that way about him.

When he tried to copy, he stole his jelly piece of him and he was a finger buster. He couldn't even play it. He put his name down and composed it. He used to play with Sidney Bichet. I don't know how to really hurt him, I guess, in New York, out on Long Island. They played with Sidney Bichet. I don't know who else. I don't know. Maybe.
